verdict_rationale.summary: The #2L large-payload retention branch FAILS the pre-registered buyer threshold (T1: ≥85% retention at 90 days) under honest first-principles physics simulation. The failure is NOT a mechanism limitation — it is a FUNDAMENTAL PHYSICS CEILING imposed by the CSF turnover rate (~2.88 turnovers/day). Even with 95% retention per pass (A1 size-selective) or strong affinity binding (A2, Kd=10^-8 M), the therapeutic is washed out over 90 days because the CSF compartment drains completely ~259 times during that period. The strongest alternative (A2 affinity-based) DOMINATES A1 (7% vs 0% for antibodies, 76% vs 0% for gene vectors) but STILL FAILS the 85% threshold. No mechanism change can overcome the CSF turnover rate — it is a physiological constant.

what_changed_from_V1.root_cause_of_discrepancy: V1 used a first-order washout model that did not properly account for the continuous CSF turnover rate of 2.88x/day. V2 uses the correct exponential decay model: C(t) = C(0) * exp(-turnover * (1-ret_eff) * t). With turnover=2.88/day, ret_eff=0.95, t=90 days: exp(-2.88*0.05*90) = exp(-12.96) ≈ 0.000002. V1's 0.488 was a MODEL ARTIFACT, not a real retention number.
what_changed_from_V1.constitution_article_applied: Article XVI — 'Never confuse implementation with proof.' V1's simulation was a hypothesis about retention. V2's first-principles physics is evidence that V1's hypothesis was wrong.

physics_ceiling_explanation.csf_turnover_rate: 2.88 turnovers/day (CSF production 0.3 mL/min × 1440 min = 432 mL/day, divided by CSF volume 150 mL)
physics_ceiling_explanation.implication: The entire CSF compartment drains and is replaced ~2.88 times per day. Over 90 days, that's ~259 complete turnovers. Even if the membrane retains 95% of the therapeutic per pass, 5% escapes each pass. After 259 passes: (0.95)^259 ≈ 0.000002 — essentially zero.
physics_ceiling_explanation.why_this_is_unengineerable: CSF production rate is a physiological constant controlled by the choroid plexus. It cannot be reduced without causing hydrocephalus (the very condition the eShunt treats). The eShunt MUST drain at ~0.3 mL/min to control ICP. Therefore the turnover rate is FIXED by the clinical indication.
physics_ceiling_explanation.what_would_overturn_this: Nothing within the current eShunt paradigm. The only way to achieve 85% retention at 90 days would be to (a) reduce CSF drainage below therapeutic levels (defeating the purpose of the shunt), or (b) use a completely different drug-delivery paradigm (e.g., implantable depot, not a membrane). Both are outside the #2L scope.

strongest_alternative_attack_result.interpretation: A2 (affinity-based) is BETTER than A1 (size-selective) for all payloads — 7% vs 0% for antibodies, 76% vs 0% for gene vectors. But A2 STILL FAILS the 85% threshold. The strongest alternative does not rescue the branch. The ceiling is physical, not mechanism-specific.
strongest_alternative_attack_result.gene_vector_near_miss: Gene vector (AAV) with Kd=10^-9 M achieves 76% retention — closest to the threshold. But this requires sub-nanomolar binding (Kd ≤ 6×10^-10 M for 85%), which is 16x stronger than typical Protein A/G. Achievable for SOME high-affinity binders but not reliably and not for all therapeutics.

constitution_compliance_check.article_II_exact_evidence: COMPLIED — first-principles physics with published physiological constants (CSF production rate, CSF volume). No fuzzy matching or approximate equality.
constitution_compliance_check.article_VII_never_weaken_verifier: COMPLIED — did not lower the 0.85 threshold to make V1's 0.488 'pass'. Did not broaden the scope to payload-agnostic. Did not introduce fuzzy retention metrics.

constitution_compliance_check.article_XIX_never_optimize_for_gate: COMPLIED — the 6-question constitutional test is answered below.
constitution_compliance_check.anti_gaming_check: PASS — no threshold lowering, no scope expansion, no model tuning, no selective reporting

constitutional_test_6_questions.q1_what_was_previously_capable_of_killin: The CSF turnover rate (2.88x/day) was always capable of killing this branch, but V1's washout model did not properly account for it. The physics was always there — V1 just didn't model it correctly.
constitutional_test_6_questions.q2_what_changed: V2 used a first-principles exponential washout model with the correct CSF turnover rate, revealing that retention at 90 days is essentially zero. V1's 0.488 was a model artifact.
constitutional_test_6_questions.q3_what_independent_evidence_shows_it_su: It did NOT survive. The branch is dead. The evidence is the physics: CSF turnover × 90 days × (1-ret_eff) = complete washout.
constitutional_test_6_questions.q4_what_is_still_capable_of_killing_it: N/A — the branch is already dead. Nothing more can kill it.
constitutional_test_6_questions.q5_what_prevents_that_attack_now: N/A — there is no attack to prevent. The ceiling is physical.
constitutional_test_6_questions.q6_did_the_fix_change_the_scientific_evi: V2 changed the MODEL (from V1's first-order washout to exponential decay), which changed the EVIDENCE (from 0.488 to 0.000). This is not 'changing the test to get a better number' — it is CORRECTING a model error to reveal the true physics. The V1 model was wrong; the V2 model is correct.

what_would_overturn_this_verdict.if_in_vitro_data_shows_csf_turnover_is_l: If actual in-vivo CSF turnover in the eShunt configuration is <0.5x/day (not 2.88x/day), retention could be higher. But this would require the eShunt to drain at <0.05 mL/min, which is far below the therapeutic drainage rate for hydrocephalus. UNLIKELY.
what_would_overturn_this_verdict.if_a_therapeutic_has_sub_nanomolar_bindi: If a therapeutic has Kd < 6×10^-10 M AND an affinity matrix exists for it, A2 could achieve 85% retention. This is a per-therapeutic question, not a general mechanism. It would be a DIFFERENT invention (affinity-based retention for a specific high-affinity therapeutic), not a continuation of #2L.
what_would_overturn_this_verdict.if_a_completely_different_paradigm_is_us: If the retention mechanism is NOT membrane-based or affinity-based but instead a depot/gel/reservoir that does not depend on CSF flow, the turnover ceiling does not apply. But this is outside the #2L scope.

branch_disposition.frozen_reason: CSF turnover rate (2.88x/day) makes 85% retention at 90 days physically impossible for any membrane-based or affinity-based mechanism. The ceiling is physiological, not engineering.
branch_disposition.patentability: MOOT — since the mechanism does not achieve buyer-grade retention, there is no buyer-relevant invention to patent. A patent on a non-functional mechanism has no commercial value.
branch_disposition.v_next_rationale: No V-next is authorized. The ceiling is physical (CSF turnover rate), not engineering. Additional simulation or benchtop testing cannot change a physiological constant.

evidence_honesty_labels.all_simulation_results: FIRST_PRINCIPLES_PHYSICS — CSF production rate (0.3 mL/min) and CSF volume (150 mL) are published physiological constants. The exponential washout model is standard pharmacokinetics. No parameter tuning.
evidence_honesty_labels.a2_kd_values: PUBLISHED_LITERATURE — Protein A/G Kd for IgG (~10^-8 M) is well-established. AAV receptor Kd (~10^-9 M) is from gene therapy literature. Nanoparticle functionalization Kd (~10^-7 M) is a conservative estimate.
evidence_honesty_labels.model_limitation: The V2 simulation assumes continuous CSF turnover. In reality, the eShunt may have a one-way valve that creates intermittent flow (drains only when ICP exceeds threshold). If drainage is intermittent rather than continuous, effective turnover could be lower. However, even at 1x/day turnover (3x lower than nominal), 90-day retention with 95% ret_eff is exp(-1*0.05*90) = exp(-4.5) = 0.011 — still far below 0.85.
evidence_honesty_labels.no_likely_novel_language: COMPLIANT — no use of 'LIKELY_NOVEL' or 'buyer-grade' without threshold passage.

impact_on_portfolio.lesson_for_future_territories: Before investing in mechanism exploration, check whether the PHYSICAL CONSTANTS of the eShunt environment (CSF turnover rate, venous pressure, flow rates) impose a ceiling. The #2L ceiling was discoverable from physiology alone — no simulation was needed to know that 2.88x/day turnover × 90 days = 259 turnovers makes membrane retention impossible. This lesson applies directly to #9 (biosensor) and #10 (predictive failure): check the physical observability ceiling before investing in the mechanism.
